description: Commands that create a `.strictmetadata` directory's `manifest.toml` while writing a record (`rlsbl release backfill`, `rlsbl release abandon`) now commit the manifest with the record instead of leaving it uncommitted
A refusing command prints no partial report: `rlsbl status` refusing a member with several targets and no `--target` no longer prints an empty status block before the error

New `rlsbl transition public-client --subject <name> --reason <text>` declares that a subject of a confidential repository has a public client, taking its registry names and the repository's names out of the confidential-name index; `transition show` lists the declarations, and the index no longer holds releasable names or identity values, nor matches a name inside a URL or a dotted hostname
`transition show` holds the confidential-names rule for a confidential repository whose public-client declarations leave it no name to protect, expecting no index entry, instead of calling it public
After a three-way merge conflict is resolved, the next `rlsbl scaffold` commits the resolved file and its new merge base, which it used to leave uncommitted.

**rlsbl is rewritten in Go.** One `rlsbl` binary replaces the Python package. It is distributed as the Go module `github.com/stricttools/rlsbl`, as npm packages under the existing `rlsbl` name (the binary in one package per platform, `rlsbl-linux-x64`, `rlsbl-linux-arm64`, `rlsbl-darwin-x64`, and `rlsbl-darwin-arm64`, selected through `optionalDependencies`), and as PyPI wheels under the existing `rlsbl` name. There are no Windows packages, and rlsbl's Python modules can no longer be imported.

**rlsbl's records move to `.strictmetadata/`.** rlsbl reads nothing of the old layout (`.rlsbl/`, `.rlsbl-monorepo/`, and each member's `.rlsbl/`). Run `rlsbl migrate records` once in every repository, with `--dry-run` first: it converts the declarations, changelogs, release files and archives, batch release files, transition record, scaffold state, hook scripts, and options entries, writes the lifecycle-and-license record (`--licenses` states a license the manifests do not), removes the old layout through saferm, and commits. `rlsbl monorepo cleanup` removes old-layout residue, in a standalone repository too.

**One declarations file.** `config.json`, `workspace.toml`, and `releasable.toml` are replaced by `.strictmetadata/releasables/releasables.toml`, declaring the layout, release branches, releasables, members, targets, pipelines, hooks, and checks; its `[timeouts]` table (`push_seconds`, `ci_seconds`, `check_seconds`, `hook_seconds`) replaces the `push_timeout`, `ci_timeout`, `check_timeout`, and `hook_timeout` keys, and behavior switches are options entries in `.strictmetadata/options/`, written with `rlsbl options set`. `rlsbl migrate records` writes both.
**The release targets are go, npm, and pypi.** The `spec` target is removed, and `rlsbl migrate records` refuses a configuration naming any target other than go, npm, and pypi, naming the hand edit.

**Changelog format version 2.** Each releasable's changelog lives in `.strictmetadata/changelog/<releasable>/`, every entry carries an id, and an entry naming more commits than the per-entry limit carries its reason through `rlsbl changelog add --batch-reason`, which replaces `--allow-batch` and the `batch_limits` exclusions; `rlsbl migrate records` restamps existing entries.

**The pre-release channel is removed.** Versions are `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`: a release file carrying `preid`, `blog`, or `bump = "prerelease"` is refused, and `rlsbl migrate records` folds a pre-release's changelog entries into the stable version it preceded.

**Removed subsystems.** Member layering (the `[layers]` key and the layers-violations check), deploy configuration (a server releasable declares a `deploy_command` instead), subtree mirror publication, the launcher artifact, local asset upload (`assets` and `custom_assets`; the publish workflow builds and attaches release archives in CI), the Cloudflare Pages pipeline (selfdoc deploys documentation sites), blog-on-release, and the `requires-services` (with the `services` and `test_env` keys), `private-hook-stale`, and `mixed-tag-schemes` checks are removed.

**Removed commands and flags.** `rlsbl deploy`, `rlsbl prs`, `rlsbl pre-push-check`, `rlsbl monorepo mirror`, `rlsbl monorepo snapshot`, `rlsbl monorepo snapshot-check` (`rlsbl monorepo graph --json` gives the same inventory on demand), `rlsbl transition record`, `rlsbl release undo --target`, and `rlsbl changelog amend --id` are removed.

**Source checks move to strictcode.** The lint, format, and type-check tool options, the dependency-declaration checks, and the dead-modules, circular-deps, library-lint, dead-workspace-packages, ruff-lint, and strictspec certificate checks leave rlsbl; the `rlsbl:strictcode` option (error by default) runs `strictcode analyze` as a release check and refuses a missing strictcode, and `rlsbl migrate records` moves their settings into `strictcode.toml`.

**The lifecycle-and-license record.** Each repository's `.strictmetadata/lifecycle-and-license/lifecycle-and-license.toml` holds each releasable's dated lifecycle, license, and identities. A release or resume of a releasable on hold or retired is refused; a proprietary releasable requires a private repository and refuses every public output (registry packages, attestations, the Go module proxy, public docs); a Go library target on a private repository is refused; and `rlsbl monorepo init`, `rlsbl monorepo add`, and `rlsbl monorepo absorb` creating a releasable require `--license`.

**Changed flags.** `rlsbl release reconcile` takes `--mode plan` or `--mode apply` instead of `--plan` and `--apply`; `rlsbl monorepo release init` requires `--releasables` or `--all`, writing no table for every releasable unasked; and `rlsbl monorepo graph` requires `--format`.
